miniProject.title: Bike demand contract, split, audits and baseline ladder
miniProject.brief: Rebuild the hourly UCI Bike Sharing demand problem in your own repository as a contract-first investigation: a one-page prediction contract, an immutable snapshot with a chronological split, an audit suite, a baseline ladder under one harness, and three seeded leakage defects that failing tests must catch. No model tuning happens until the contract and ladder are frozen.
steps: Write the contract for next-hour `cnt`: unit, prediction time, cutoff, horizon, served action, misprediction costs, and an availability table for `hour.csv` marking same-hour weather as oracle-forecast and `casual` and `registered` prohibited, with the feedback loop kept as a monitored exclusion.

Store `hour.csv` with its hash and download date. Build the chronological split of early years to train and the later year to test, asserting no test timestamp precedes train and no prohibited column reaches features.

Write the audit suite covering schema and `dtypes`, missingness, keys and duplicates, time continuity, ranges and normalizations, rare categories and availability. Seed one defect per audit in a copy and show each test fails.

Build the baseline ladder in one harness scored by RMSE: train mean, train median, train-last constant, previous row and a label-free linear model, checked against scikit-learn, stating which rung a new model must beat and why.

Seed three leakage defects: global scaling before the split, the target-derived `casual` and `registered` features, and cross-partition duplicates (copy 500 test rows into train). Catch each with a failing test, report the score before and after repair, and score the contaminated rows separately.

Wrap preprocessing in a `ColumnTransformer` pipeline fitted on train only, write the lineage record (source URL, hash, split rule, seeds, library versions), and run a joblib round trip that asserts identical predictions on five probe rows.
deliverables: `contract.md` with the availability table, the declared assumptions, the cost statement and the feedback note.
The data package: snapshot manifest, split builder and audit suite with its seeded-defect tests.
The ladder report: one table of rungs with RMSE and the verdict on whether complexity is justified.
The leakage casebook: three defects, each with its failing test, its repair and the conclusion it changed.

rubric.pass: Every column is classified with a reason, and prediction time, cutoff and horizon are stated.
rubric.strong: The oracle-forecast assumption is priced: the linear rung is rerun without same-hour weather and the change is reported.

rubric.pass: The split is chronological with no prohibited column, and every audit fails on its seeded defect.
rubric.strong: One command runs all audits, and a property test shows the split builder never places a test row before a train row.

rubric.pass: All five rungs land within a few RMSE points of the reference under one harness.
rubric.strong: The report explains why the previous row wins, and why the median loses to the mean on the later test period.

rubric.pass: Three defects are each caught by a failing test, with scores before and after repair.
rubric.strong: The casebook shows a defect the score cannot reveal (scaler leakage leaves a least-squares RMSE unchanged) and one that only the separately scored rows expose.

rubric.pass: The lineage record is complete and the joblib round trip passes.
rubric.strong: A fresh clone rebuilds every reported number with one command.

miniProject.feedsInto: Milestone artifact 1, the contract and leakage pack: the contract, manifest, split builder, audits, the naive baselines and the preserved leakage failure come from here.
